text.p: Italian debt markets climbed amid a positive bond market environment, with Btp futures ending up near the day's highs.

One London-based broker said the main booster for the market had been the dollar, which allowed the lira to firm to 977.10 per mark from 983.90 earlier in the day. U.S. jobs data also indicated a U.S. economy growing reasonably without undue inflation pressures, which helped the market, dealers said.
On the European front, a conciliatory meeting between German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi calmed some nervousness over Italy's chances for EMU entry.
"Prodi and Kohl had a role in all this but it was one to calm the markets down -- sort of no news being good news," one broker said.

The March Btp future on LIFFE was 94 basis points up at 131.28 after hitting the day's peak at 131.35 earlier. The November 2006 Btp was 33 basis points up and yielding 7.16 percent with a 154 basis point spread over the benchmark Bund.

Prodi said for Italy to get into shape to meet the EMU criteria was tougher for Germany but he was more confident than he was a few weeks ago. "There is no possibility that Italy will not be there for consideration for currency union on time."
Kohl for his part said Germany would not take part in making judgements on who would join, a year before the decision needs to be taken, describing such speculation as "unacceptable".

Back on EMU basics, Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said in a newspaper interview that if Italy needed to pass a mini-budget, he expected it to amount to no more than one percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP). His remarks, which suggest an eventual mini-budget of 19-20 trillion lire, are the first official comment on the possible size of any such package. Prodi has said any decision on a possible mini-budget will be made in late February or early March. --C.Cooper, Milan +392 66129507
